title: Model: multi-period selection with all section 6 rules

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A planner asks for section 6's carry-over budget rule in CIPT Lite, but the export carries no carry-over rate. What does the milestone's model do with a rule whose data the snapshot lacks?

options.text: Adds the rule with a rate of zero, so that it is present but cannot bind
options.says: A row with a number nobody exported is a row with invented numbers, which the lesson rules out.

options.text: Adds the rule with the rate from the section 6 lesson's own example
options.says: That rate would be invented for this portfolio too; the lesson leaves such rules out.

options.text: Adds the rule as a penalty in the objective, so that it can bend when needed
options.says: Nothing in the model is a penalty; the lesson leaves rules without data out.

options.text: Leaves the rule out and says so, since its row would need invented numbers
options.says: Right: "A rule without its data would be a row with invented numbers, so CIPT Lite leaves them out and says so."

origin.section: Every Rule GridCap's Data Carries Is a Named Row

questions.stem: With the run setting, a model reports OPTIMAL, NPV $100,000k and bound $100,080k. A colleague solves the same model to a zero gap and gets $100,060k. What does this say about the run?

options.text: It is wrong, since OPTIMAL should mean that no better plan exists
options.says: Under a gap, OPTIMAL means proved within the gap, not the best plan; the lesson's own run was $154k below the zero-gap plan.

options.text: It is within its stated tolerance, since its NPV is within 0.1% of the reference
options.says: Right: 100,060 x 0.999 = 99,960, and 100,000 is above it, which is the milestone's "within tolerance".

options.text: It shows the zero-gap solve is wrong, since no plan can beat an OPTIMAL one
options.says: The zero-gap solve is the reference; the run setting's OPTIMAL allows plans up to 0.1% below the best.

options.text: It shows the two solves used different models, since one model has one optimal value
options.says: The lesson solved one model both ways and got $219,054k and $219,208k, both OPTIMAL.

origin.section: A Run Stops at a Stated Gap, and Its Plan Is Checked Without the Model

questions.stem: A refactor halves every crew limit by mistake, so the crew rows are twice as strict as the data. Which of the lesson's tests catches it?

options.text: Checking the solver's plan with check(), since a too-strict row gives a plan that breaks a rule
options.says: A plan that obeys stricter rows obeys the data's rules too; the lesson says a too-strict rule is something no check of the solver's own plans can reveal.

options.text: The plans built to break one rule, since each of them tests one row of the model
options.says: The lesson says a row made stricter still refuses every plan built to break it, so the refused side cannot catch a rule that is too strict.

options.text: A valid hand-built plan that the model must allow, since a too-strict row refuses it
options.says: Right: the allowed side catches a rule that is too strict, which no check of the solver's plans can reveal.

options.text: None of them, since a stricter rule still refuses every plan that it should refuse
options.says: The allowed side exists for exactly this case: a valid plan must pass, or a rule is too strict.

origin.section: Hand-Built Plans Test Each Rule From Both Sides
